title: Balance - imbalance: toward a systemic understanding of life distress
abstract: Despite extensive research efforts, biomedical psychiatry has struggled to provide sufficiently valid, reliable and comprehensive explanations for life distress. This has contributed to increasing international calls for broader and more contextual approaches to mental health. In this article, I propose as systemic and practice-informed framework for understanding life distress in terms of relationships, pattern, meaning and context. Drawing on systems theory, feedback-informed clinical practice and contemporary critiques of diagnostic psychiatry, the article introduces the balance-imbalance model as a heuristic framework for understanding distress as emerging within complex and interacting systems rather than isolated pathological entities. The article situates itself within ongoing debates concerning biomedical, ecological, phenomenological and relational approaches to mental health. Rather than presenting distress as evidence of underlying disease categories, the proposed framework conceptualizes imbalance as a dynamic process arising through interactions between biological, psychological, relational, social and cultural factors. Healing is correspondingly understood as processes through which individuals and their environments may move toward more sustainable forms of balance. A clinical case example is used to illustrate how a systemic and contextual understanding may open alternative pathways for understanding and responding to severe distress beyond diagnostic categorization. The balance–imbalance model is presented not as a universal explanatory theory, but as a conceptual and clinical orientation intended to support more holistic, collaborative and context-sensitive approaches to mental health practice. The article discusses implications for clinical work, research, education and policy development, and argues for greater integration of lived experience, relational knowledge and practice-based evidence within mental health services.
